findings.expected: Every authored question says 'Show the working used'. Under that instruction, and under the explicit general NSSCAS rule 8227:CONVENTION:076 ('No marks are awarded if only answers are given', reports 2021 PDF236, 2022 PDF307, 2023 PDF330, 2024 PDF335/printed333, verified on the rendered 2024 page), an unsupported numeric gradient or bare normal equation earns 0. The official 2025 P2 Q5 G5 is A1 C.A.O. following method marks, not a free-standing answer mark.
findings.actual: Answer-only numeric gradient earns G5 (1/5); a bare exact normal equation earns N1+N2 (2/7), i.e. an M mark with no method seen; the 'Ambiguous' sample repeats 'Numeric-only -24/5 earns 1/5'.
findings.evidence: Exemplar question text 'Show the working used'; marking-conventions.json rule 076 (explicit general rule, application_years 2021-2025); report 2025 PDF359 table.
findings.repair: Set answer-only to 0/5 and 0/2 (or, if the owner wants a concession, a capped SC that is explicitly an owner departure from 076 and drop 'Show the working used'). Never award N1 (M) without the perpendicular-gradient step seen.

findings.expected: NSSCAS 076: no marks for answers only; the 2021/2023/2024 reports specifically cite calculators that differentiate or solve cubics, and the 2024 Paper 2 general comment requires the factorisation or quadratic-formula substitution to be shown. Stationary coordinates of a cubic are exactly calculator-obtainable output.
findings.actual: 'Coordinates alone earn P3/P4=2/4'; 'A correct coordinate alone earns I3=1/3'; P2 M1 'solve f'=0' does not require the factorisation/formula to be visible. No reference to rule 076 is given for this departure.
findings.evidence: marking-conventions.json 8227:CONVENTION:076 and :002; rendered report 2024 PDF335 (printed 333); 2021 P1 Q11(a) award DM1 'solve equation =0' (PDF234).
findings.repair: Make answer-only coordinates 0 (or an owner-approved capped SC citing the departure), and state that P2/I2 require the factorised or formula step of f'=0 to be seen.

findings.expected: A first-derivative sign test alone (f'(h)=0 and f' of the same sign at stated points either side, or the perfect-square argument f'=3a(x-h)^2 not changing sign) fully classifies a polynomial stationary point as a stationary inflexion (an even-multiplicity root of f' forces f'' to change sign), and is the method the work order says it adopted: YM Example 27 (PDF298) concludes 'stationary point of inflexion' from the dy/dx sign table alone. The syllabus says 'distinguish (by any method)' (PDF12) and 2025 P1 Q9(c) prose (report PDF351) accepts 'd2A/dx2 or ... the signs of dA/dx'. Such work must earn I5+I6.
findings.actual: The canonical reasoning says f' signs only exclude max/min 'while f'' changes sign across h, establishing a stationary inflexion'; the criteria row says 'A coherent first-derivative test plus explicit concavity evidence is accepted'; no sentence credits the f'-sign route on its own. A marker or oracle built from this text would withhold I6 from learners using the textbook/NSSCAS method.
findings.evidence: YM-298 render; syllabus PDF12; report 2025 PDF351; sympy check that all 180 admitted instances have f' of constant sign either side of h and f'' sign change.
findings.repair: State explicitly that I5+I6 are each earned by ANY one of: (i) f' sign either side (values or perfect-square argument) with conclusion; (ii) f'' sign change across h with f'(h)=0; (optionally iii) f'''(h)≠0 after f''(h)=0. Concavity evidence is not additionally required. Add a sample submission using route (i) earning 6/6.

findings.expected: Bloom 4 (Analyse) needs the learner to make a discriminating decision the marking requires. PLAN says the branch should 'Distinguish extrema from a genuine stationary inflexion'.
findings.actual: The prompt itself tells the learner to examine 'whether the value of the second derivative at the stationary point settles its type'; every one of the 180 instances has one stationary point and the identical outcome (always a stationary inflexion; quartic flat extrema excluded), so no instance requires distinguishing; I4 is recall of a taught rule and I5/I6 apply the taught sign test (YM PDF298-299). The BLOOM-CLASSIFICATION policy says to classify the assessed work, not a cue or command word.
findings.evidence: Exhaustive enumeration (all 180 same classification); exemplar question wording lines 43,55,67.
findings.repair: Either label classification Apply (3) and the branch maximum 3, or redesign for genuine analysis: remove the cue and mix in admitted a(x-h)^4+c instances (power rule, in scope) where f''(h)=0 but the point is a max/min, so the learner must decide; then re-review Bloom.

findings.expected: Capacity statements count distinct underlying models correctly (the log recipe in the same paragraph counts models, not presentations).
findings.actual: 'The implicit branches share the same 42 underlying curves' -- there are 36 distinct curves. Because (y-q)(y+q+a)=0 at x=0, each curve passes through (0,q) and (0,-q-a); for (3,k,-1)/(3,k,-2) and (4,k,-1)/(4,k,-3), k=1..3, both are admitted, giving 6 curves used twice (different point, different gradient). All 6 positive-gradient tasks lie on these shared curves.
findings.repair: Say '42 point-tasks on 36 curves'; decide whether no-repeat identity is the curve or the (curve, point) pair; if the curve, drop one point of each pair.
